Social Security recipients typically receive their payments on the second, third, and fourth Wednesdays of the month.

However, there are a few exceptions, as payments administered by the Social Security Administration may fall on different dates.

For example, Veterans' Day, Nov. 11, falls on the second Wednesday of the month. Because of the holiday, recipients will receive their benefits on Tuesday, Nov. 10.

Here's what to know about this year's payments.

To be eligible for Social Security retirement benefits, you must be at least 62 years old and have earned at least 40 work credits — this is equal to about 10 years of work while paying Social Security taxes.

Beyond retirement, you may be eligible for Social Security benefits if you are disabled or blind and meet specific medical and work-credit criteria. Family members such as spouses, ex-spouses, survivors, dependent parents, and children of eligible workers may also qualify for payments. In that case, your payment would be based on the primary beneficiary's birthday.

Who is eligible for Supplemental Security Income benefits?

Supplemental Security Income, which is also administered by the Social Security Administration, provides monthly payments to people with disabilities and older adults who have little or no income or resources.

In some cases, retirees may qualify for Social Security benefits based on their work history, as well as SSI benefits due to their financial need.

Those who qualify for SSI include adults and children who have:

A disability, blindness, or are age 65 or older.

According to the Social Security Administration (SSA), payments are distributed based on the recipient's birth date. Typically, they arrive on the second, third, and fourth Wednesdays of each month.

Exactly which Wednesday will depend on your birth date.

Recipients who are born from the first to the 10th of the month receive their benefit on the second Wednesday of the month. If your birth date falls on the 11th to the 20th of the month, you'll receive your payment on the third Wednesday of the month. Those who are born on the 21st to the 31st of the month will receive their payment on the fourth Wednesday of the month.

Supplemental Security Income benefits are usually paid on the first of the month. If the first falls on a weekend or holiday, the payment is made on the preceding business day.

A full schedule of this year's Social Security payments is available on the Social Security Administration's website.

If your friend has received her Social Security check this month, but you haven't, there's no need to panic.

Payments are sent out in bundles based on birthdays, and for most people, they're electronically deposited directly into a federally insured bank account.

By law, all federal benefit payments — including Social Security and Supplemental Security Income benefits — must be made electronically with few exceptions. Your monthly benefit is either sent to your bank account via direct deposit or loaded onto a Direct Express Debit Mastercard. If you're applying for Social Security or Supplemental Security Income benefits, you can elect to receive your benefit payment in one of these methods electronically when you enroll .

If you currently receive Social Security or Supplemental Security Income benefits by check, you are in the minority and may need to switch to an electronic payment option if possible.

Direct deposits typically appear by 9 a.m. on your payment day. If your payment is late, check with your bank or financial institution to see if there has been a posting delay.

If you receive your benefits by paper check, it can take up to three business days to receive your benefits. If that doesn't happen, contact the SSA via phone at 800-772-1213, or online through your My Social Security account.

Your My Social Security account is a free personalized portal where you can request a replacement Social Security card, check the status of a benefits application, estimate future benefits, or manage the benefits you already receive. You can set up an account even if you don't currently receive benefits.

Confirm that the SSA has your correct bank information and address, and it's a good idea to sign up for SSA to notify you when the payment is sent out.

You can apply to start your Social Security checks via your My Social Security account or make an appointment with an agent in person or by phone at 800-333-1795. You select the month you want your benefit to start in your application. After you apply, SSA will send you a letter confirming that your benefits are approved or that you need to provide more information.

It typically takes at least a month to receive your first Social Security check after your application is processed. The precise timing of your payment delivery relies on processing times at the Social Security Administration. Right now, staffing cuts and other backend tech disruptions are raising alarms.

During an SSA operations meeting in April , an official from the agency reported that the field offices "are struggling right now to keep pace with the timeliness this year."

That's why it's smart to apply up to four months before you want to start receiving benefits.

As Jason Fichtner, executive director of the Retirement Income Institute who served in several positions at the Social Security Administration, warned in an interview: "With SSA staff being reduced while the agency was already operating at insufficient support levels and computer systems in need of modernization, continued service delays, and breakdowns are likely."

LONDON, Nov 3 (Reuters) - Oil prices slumped on Tuesday after President Donald Trump said the US would end billions of dollars of annual military support to Israel.

Prices had ‌earlier risen after an Iranian official said Tehran and Washington remained far from a deal ‌to end their war and the US struck Iran's Qeshm Island.

Brent crude futures were down $3.45, or 3.3%, to $101.32 a barrel at 1350 ​GMT. They hit their lowest since October 8 during the session, having earlier traded above $107 a barrel.

US West Texas Intermediate crude was down $2.16, or 2.2%, to 94.30 a barrel, having earlier his its lowest since October 15.

"Now, as far as paying Israel, Bibi Netanyahu and I have made a deal that we give Israel $4 billion a ‌year, and we made a deal ⁠months ago that we're stopping," Trump told Fox News' Fox and Friends. "We've already agreed that by the end of this year we won't be paying Israel."

Both benchmarks dropped ⁠more than 7% on Monday as talks between Iranian and Qatari officials lifted hopes for an end to the US-Israeli war with Iran.

Qatar's foreign ministry spokesperson said on Tuesday that the US and Iran remain committed to mediation ​efforts ​and are reviewing proposals aimed at bridging their differences. Talks ​with both sides had shown progress and ‌efforts to narrow remaining gaps were continuing, the spokesperson added.

"Despite these positive signals, it's probably too early to think escalation risks have passed," ING said in a note on Tuesday. "What is clear, though, is that strong signals of progress in peace talks would mean more downside for prices."

Polls open across the US on Tuesday in midterm elections that will serve as a referendum on Trump's first two years back in office, ‌with voter frustration over the Iran war and the resulting ​rise in fuel prices emerging as a key issue.

Brent ended October ​at its highest in six months on ​concerns the conflict could escalate again after the elections.

A Ukrainian drone attack, meanwhile, damaged ‌an oil refinery in the Russian city of ​Yaroslavl, Governor Mikhail Evrayev said ​on Tuesday.

Russia launched a massive overnight strike on Ukrainian energy facilities in the Vinnytsia, Dnipropetrovsk and Kharkiv regions, Interfax news agency said, citing the defence ministry.

articles.title: Energy Transfer Approves $1.6 Billion Gas Pipe as AI Use Soars
articles.summary: Energy Transfer LP formally committed to building a $1.6 billion pipeline that will move natural gas from eastern Louisiana across Mississippi, a move that c...
articles.body:
(Bloomberg) -- Energy Transfer LP formally committed to building a $1.6 billion pipeline that will move natural gas from eastern Louisiana across Mississippi, a move that comes as data centers and export terminals boost demand for the fuel.

The 215-mile (346-kilometer) South Mississippi Pipeline project will have the capacity to ship as much as 1.2 billion cubic feet of gas per day, the company said in a statement Tuesday. Energy Transfer expects to operate the project and own 51%, with the rest of the stake coming from customers.

The project will "give shippers greater access to natural gas from multiple basins across the southeastern US," according to the statement.

Energy Transfer and other pipeline operators are rushing to put gas conduits into service as consumption of the fuel soars, driven by liquefied natural gas export terminals along the Gulf Coast and new power plants serving AI data centers. The infrastructure boom is stoking concern that the data center buildout will undo 15 years worth of greenhouse gas reductions from US electricity generation.

The Dallas-based company's shares rose 0.8% before the start of regular trading in New York.

Energy Transfer is holding a binding open season for additional customer commitments to the project, which is set to end Nov. 25. The pipeline is expected to start up in 2030.

Energy Transfer also added equipment to boost gas flows on its Rover Pipeline system in the Midwest, which the expansion coming online Nov. 1, according to the statement. It also entered into two agreements to provide 150,000 million British thermal units per day of gas transportation to two power plants under construction in Missouri.

articles.title: Prediction markets vs. polls: Election forecasting industry faces midterm test
articles.summary: Prediction markets and pollsters both say Democrats are favored to take both the US House and Senate on Tuesday.
articles.body:
Prediction markets and pollsters both say Democrats are favored to take both the US House and Senate in the midterms. Prediction markets have been a little less certain about it, though traders' odds jumped on Tuesday on the chances of Democrats taking control of the Senate.

That's setting up what could be another chapter in the burgeoning rivalry between prediction markets and polls following 2024's closely watched results.

The differences have been most evident in the upper chamber. A small but consistent gap has been evident for months in the odds of Democrats winning control of the Senate. The gap has averaged about 7.3 percentage points since Sept. 1, according to a Yahoo Finance analysis.

But the gap has narrowed approaching Election Day, closing to 2.9 percentage points on Tuesday morning. Three prediction markets place a 77.3% chance of Democrats taking control, while two polling-based models put the chances a bit higher at 80.2%.

The odds have been a bit more evenly matched around the House of Representatives, with an average gap of less than a percentage point in recent months.

The latest read on Tuesday showed a 2.2-percentage-point gap, with prediction markets suggesting a 94% chance of Democrats flipping the chamber, versus 96.2% odds from polls.

This analysis was conducted by averaging the daily odds from three leading prediction markets, Kalshi, Polymarket, and PredictIt, to create one rolling prediction market measure. Those values were then compared to the average of two leading poll-focused models — one from statistician Nate Silver and another from Harvard called ElectIt.

These gaps have had an outsized effect on public perceptions in recent years.

This was especially true in 2024, when a 10-percentage-point difference between prediction markets and polls led to some post-election analyses claiming that prediction markets had gotten the results right and polls had gotten them wrong.

The stakes for prediction market companies are high. Kalshi and Polymarket have long argued that their markets are more truthful than polls because market participants have money on the line. The markets also had a high-profile miss recently when the winner of Brazil's presidential election was given just 20% odds before ultimately prevailing.

The scrutiny also comes as these markets continue to grow rapidly. Kalshi shared new data over the weekend that more than $1.2 billion has now been traded on midterm markets, surpassing the platform's volume during the 2024 presidential election.

articles.title: Crowdstrike says it will buy two AI cybersecurity startups, announces 'kill switch' for AI agents
articles.summary: CrowdStrike has agreed to buy two AI security startups for a combined purchase price of $495 million, according to the Wall Street Journal.
articles.body:
What happened: CrowdStrike ( CRWD ) said Tuesday that it has agreed to buy two AI security startups. The combined purchase price for both is $495 million , according to the Wall Street Journal. Shares of the cybersecurity company gained more than 2% in early trading.

What's behind the move: CrowdStrike said it has signed an agreement to acquire Fiddler AI, a startup that develops tools that help companies track their AI systems.

The company also announced an agreement to acquire Dreadnode, a startup that develops tools to test AI systems for security vulnerabilities. CrowdStrike said the technology will allow its Falcon platform to continuously scan AI models, applications, and agents for potential security weaknesses before they are deployed.

What else you need to know: The company also announced the AI Kill Switch in Falcon Guardian , giving security teams control over AI agents. If an agent deviates from its intended behavior, a defender can terminate it wherever it runs, prevent it from launching again, and cut off its enterprise network access.

"AI safety is how you get the full benefit of AI. When you deploy agents with a kill switch, you stay in control," said George Kurtz, CEO and founder of CrowdStrike, in a press release.

Despite concerns earlier this year that AI would disrupt traditional business models, cybersecurity companies have instead benefited from the rise of agentic AI, which is driving increased demand for verification and authentication.

articles.title: Job openings and hiring edged higher in September, but it's still a 'low hire, low fire' market
articles.summary: Job openings and hiring showed slight signs of improvement in September, though the job market remains sluggish.
articles.body:
Job openings and hiring changed little in September, the Labor Department's monthly Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey showed, as the "low hire, low fire" labor market continued.

There were 7.5 million job openings in September, from a revised 7.2 million a month earlier, the report showed. The hiring rate improved slightly to 3.4%, up from 3.3% in September.

Layoffs were also little changed at 1.6 million, with 1% of workers losing their jobs. Voluntary quits ticked up slightly to 3.4 million, and the rate of quits rose slightly to 2.1%, from 1.9% in August.

The latest data suggest a continuation of a long labor market trend of slow hiring, but minimal layoffs. A fuller look at the job market will be released on Friday, when the Bureau of Labor Statistics publishes its monthly payrolls report for October. Economists surveyed by Bloomberg expect the US to have added 65,000 jobs last month.

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.summary: Happiest Minds–ITC Infotech merger to close by Sep-Oct 2027; share swap and new listing expected Nov 2027, pending CCI approvals; combined Rs 7,033 crore.
articles.body: BengaluruThe merger of Happiest Minds Technologies with ITC Infotech is expected to be completed by September-October 2027, with the share swap and listing of new shares likely in November next year, Happiest Minds managing director Venkatraman Narayanan said. The company is awaiting regulatory clearances from Competition Commission of India (CCI), while the Saudi competition authority has acknowledged its application.ITC Infotech is acquiring Ashok Soota-promoted Happiest Minds, creating India’s 11th largest IT services player, with combined revenue of Rs 7,033 crore and a workforce of 19,000 across the US, Europe, the Middle East, APAC and India.The transaction will see ITC Infotech acquire a 22.1% minority stake in Happiest Minds from the promoter and promoter entities, Ashok Soota and Ashok Soota Medical Research, in two tranches for Rs 1,330 crore, at an average price of about Rs 395 per share.Following regulatory clearances, the first transaction will take place, with an ITC nominee joining the Happiest Minds board. The company had explored the reverse structure, but it was not feasible under the prevailing regulatory framework.On whether Happiest Minds would retain its brand identity, Narayanan said the decision would be part of discussions with ITC. He pointed to previous acquisitions such as Yoga Bar and 24 Mantra, which have retained their brands.Addressing concerns over job losses, co-chairman and CEO Joseph Anantharaju said ITC management had assured employees there would be roles for everyone in the merged entity. “The commitment from the ITC management, starting from the chairman of ITC, is that he wants to see everybody becoming part of the merged entity,” he said.While some role adjustments, particularly at senior levels, could happen, Anantharaju said the larger employment challenge for the technology industry was adapting to AI. “The real fear that people should have with respect to job losses is the reorientation that’s required from each and every one of us from AI and its onslaught,” Narayanan said.On business performance, Narayanan said revenue growth remained a concern despite improved profitability. articles.title: HOA fees have spiked over 50% in the last 4 years. Insurance and utilities are to blame.
articles.summary: HOA fees have risen at twice the rate of overall inflation in recent years, driven by factors like insurance.
articles.body:
Homeowners association dues have risen at roughly twice the rate of broader inflation as communities contend with the ballooning costs of insuring and maintaining their properties.

Vantaca, an HOA management software company, found in a new report that assessments rose nearly 51% between 2021 and 2025. HOAs' insurance costs were a major contributor to the higher fees, jumping 75%, while utilities rose 63%. Maintenance, which is typically the largest expense for HOAs, jumped by a comparatively modest 26%.

The new data underscores the extent to which this major "hidden cost of homeownership" has risen, pressuring the budgets of the nearly 80 million Americans who live in HOA or condo association communities.

"Insurance is such a meaningful contributor in most geographies," Vantaca CEO Ben Currin said in an interview. "We've seen over the past five years increasing natural disasters, wildfires, and hurricanes in the Southeast. The ripple through into renewals and carriers exiting markets [has been] such a big contributor to rising costs, especially in condos."

Association fees — and what they cover — vary widely by community. Neighborhoods of single-family homes tend to have lower dues that fund shared neighborhood amenities like parks and pools. Condominium buildings, in contrast, usually have much higher fees because they have far more shared spaces and systems to insure and maintain.

While costs are up across all types of associations, condo owners have felt more pain: Their assessments rose 96% between 2021 and 2025, compared with a 49% jump for single-family home communities.

Special assessment bills — one-time fees separate from regular dues that often cover major maintenance projects or unexpected shortfalls — are also substantially larger for condo owners, averaging $1,450 per condo in 2025, compared with $514 for the typical single-family home.

As housing affordability continues to deteriorate, many prospective and current homeowners are taking a closer look at their HOA fees and special assessments. The high fees that come with older condos in particular have contributed to higher inventory and sinking demand for those units in many cities, experts have told Yahoo Finance.

Vantaca found that nearly 40% of homeowners think their dues are too high, but 73% would accept an increase in their fees if the rationale was clearly explained to them.

Many, though, say they feel like they're in the dark about their community's financial situation — fewer than 1 in 5 homeowners say they get all the information they need about an association's finances and operations.

"This is a major expense for these folks, and they feel like it's a little bit of a black box when they don't have access to all the right information," Currin said.

Claire Boston is a senior reporter for Yahoo Finance covering housing, mortgages, and home insurance.

articles.title: I bonds are back: Why the new 5.51% rate is so attractive
articles.summary: The annualized yield for new I bond purchases made through April is now 5.51%, up from the 4.26%, the Treasury Department announced on Friday.
articles.body:
Series I savings bond purchases perked up in two key ways this month.

First, the annualized yield for new I bond purchases made through April is now 5.51%, up from the 4.26% annual return in effect since May, the Treasury Department announced on Friday.

Compared with other savings options on the market, like CDs, high-yield savings accounts, and short-term Treasurys, that rate is appealing.

I bonds had lost some luster from the heady days when they were wildly popular amid soaring inflation, which pushed the annualized rate to 7.12% in November 2021 and a record 9.62% in May 2022.

The second reason new I bond purchases just got better: They have a new fixed rate of 1.40%, up from 0.90%. The fixed rate applies for the life of the bond and is added to the I bond inflation rate, which changes every six months based on current inflation.

The annualized rate, or composite/earnings rate, for an I bond is calculated by combining the fixed rate and the semiannual variable inflation rate.

The Treasury Department resets interest rates for Series I bonds on Nov. 1 and May 1, and at times when inflation is top of mind, people pay attention to these changes. The date you buy your I bonds dictates your returns.

Your retirement savings need to keep up with inflation, which is hovering around 3.7% and has risen in six of the past eight months. Series I bonds are built to do just that.

"For those interested in I bonds for the long term, the fixed rate is much more important than the variable inflation rate, which changes every six months," Ken Tumin, co-founder of DepositQuest.com , a blog that tracks I bond rates, among other deposit accounts, told Yahoo Finance.

"The fixed rate remains with the I bond until it's redeemed or until it reaches its 30-year maturity. It ensures that the I bond value will grow above inflation."

I bonds can be purchased in allotments of $25 or more when you buy them electronically from the US Treasury's website, TreasuryDirect , with no fee. Paper bonds are sold in five denominations: $50, $100, $200, $500, and $1,000.

Normally, you can't buy more than $10,000 in I bonds each calendar year, but there are a couple of ways to bump up that amount. For instance, you can direct your federal tax refund to buy an additional $5,000 in I bonds.

The interest is generally free from state and local taxes. If you qualify, you might also be able to avoid federal income tax if you use the interest to pay qualified higher education expenses in the same calendar year you redeem the eligible I bonds.

articles.title: Widow faced tax demand over Rs 60 lakh cash deposit in her bank account; ITAT Pune accepts explanation that it was a gift from husband and deletes addition
articles.summary: Your husband deposits money in your account as a gift for you and your daughters but then passes away. Are you liable to pay tax on the deposit?
articles.body: Your husband deposits money in your account as a gift for you and your daughters but then passes away. Are you liable to pay tax on the deposit?In one such case the Income Tax Department sent a notice to a widow treating a cash deposit of Rs 60 lakh as unexplained income. However, the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) Pune ruled in her favour.The case underlines why taxpayers should retain relevant documents to substantiate the source of money in their bank accounts.What the case is aboutThe Income Tax Department discovered that a woman's bank account had seen a cash deposit of Rs 60,07,500 during the financial year 2015-16. However, she had not filed an income tax return (ITR) for the corresponding assessment year.The Assessing Officer (AO) subsequently issued a show-cause notice under Section 148A(b) of the Income Tax Act, 1961. As the woman did not respond, the AO passed an order.The department then sent further notices asking her to furnish details about the cash deposits. Since no documentary evidence had been provided, the AO issued another show-cause notice, seeking an explanation for why the assessment should not be completed on the basis of the information already available on record.The widow responded by filing her ITR in 2024, declaring a total income of Rs 12,000. Along with the return, she submitted an explanation that the Rs 60 lakh deposited in her account was a gift from her deceased husband. She also explained that she had been unable to collect the necessary documents.According to the woman, her husband died in 2023. He had deposited the money in her bank account as a gift intended for her and their two minor daughters.The widow maintained that the Rs 60 lakh deposited in her bank account was a gift from her late husband intended for the family, including their two minor daughters. She argued that the amount should not be treated as taxable income in her hands.The Assessing Officer, however, pointed out that the assessee’s bank account contained unexplained credits totalling Rs 75 lakh. These comprised a cash deposit of Rs 60 lakh and clearing cheque credits of Rs 15 lakh. Since the woman had not furnished evidence establishing the source of the cash, the AO treated the Rs 60 lakh as unexplained money and added it to her income under Section 69A.The woman’s counsel submitted that she was a housewife who had never filed an income tax return because she had no independent source of income.To substantiate her explanation, Ms Parve furnished several documents, including Form 26AS, an affidavit, her husband's death certificate, a computation sheet and bank statements.Why did ITAT rule in the widow’s favour?The tribunal considered that the woman’s husband, who had allegedly gifted the Rs 60 lakh to her and their two minor daughters, had passed away and was therefore no longer available to provide a confirmation, affidavit or explanation regarding the transaction.It also observed that the widow had met the initial burden of establishing the donor's identity and her relationship with him. The documents and explanations submitted included his PAN details and confirmations from their two daughters regarding the gift.The woman was able to explain the source of the money and establish her relationship with the person who had given it to her. She submitted her late husband's death certificate and PAN details, along with her own affidavit and confirmations from both daughters.Explaining the significance of the evidence, Advocate Shourya Garg, Founder of Garg & Garg Tax Associates, told ET: “The Tribunal said she had done enough to prove the donor's identity and the relationship, and the department had not shown her documents to be false. It also did not accept that section 69A means an automatic addition,”With her husband no longer alive to personally confirm the transaction, the tribunal accepted her explanation that the money had been gifted by him and ordered the deletion of the addition.Accepting the explanation that the Rs 60 lakh cash deposit represented a gift from her late husband to her and their two daughters, the tribunal concluded that the addition under Section 69A was not justified. ITAT Pune accordingly directed the AO to delete the addition of Rs 60 lakh.Garg advised people to begin collecting the relevant paperwork as early as possible, while documents and details of past transactions are still accessible. Important records to preserve include the deceased person's death certificate and legal heir certificate, bank statements, passbooks, fixed deposit receipts, previous income tax returns and PAN details.If the deceased family member had given you money or made gifts, maintain a written record of the transactions, including their dates and amounts. Garg said that a straightforward, signed gift letter and written confirmations from other family members could prove useful if questions arise later.He also recommended registering as a legal heir on the income tax portal to access the deceased person's tax filings. For gifts made in the future, he advised using bank transfers instead of cash.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Wright: ‘The best cure for high prices is high prices’
articles.summary: Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Tuesday that high energy prices will soon come down, citing a boost in U.S. production. During an interview on Fox Business’s “Big Money in the Morning,” Wright said the Trump administration is “working with” producers to “restart” operations at closed fuel refineries and expand established operations. “This is what capitalism’s…
articles.body:
Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Tuesday that high energy prices will soon come down, citing a boost in U.S. production.

During an interview on Fox Business’s “ Big Money in the Morning ,” Wright said the Trump administration is “working with” producers to “restart” operations at closed fuel refineries and expand established operations.

“This is what capitalism’s all about. The markets are sending that price mechanism as well,” he added. “Prices are high. The best cure for high prices is high prices, it grows supply.”

Higher prices typically encourage producers to supply more energy, which in turn will drive prices down.

Gas and diesel prices have risen in the U.S. amid the Iran war , as the Islamic Republic’s restrictions on shipping in the Strait of Hormuz have hampered the energy industry.

Gas and diesel cost an average of $4.15 per gallon and about $6.29 per gallon, respectively, according to AAA .

Higher fuel prices pose a political problem for the GOP, as voters on Tuesday will determine which party controls Congress for the bulk of President Trump’s final two years in office.

Patrick De Haan, the head of petroleum analysis at GasBuddy, wrote Tuesday on the social platform X that the national average prices for gas and diesel set a “new election day record.”

But Wright had an optimistic view on Tuesday , saying exports of refined products out of the Persian Gulf are increasing.

The Energy chief also said energy production in India and the U.S. will rise, predicting prices will subsequently decline.

“Gasoline and diesel prices peaked in September, they’re on their way down, and they will continue down meaningfully in the months ahead,” he said.

articles.title: Google will let schools turn off AI, but they may also lose Search
articles.summary: Google is rolling out new controls for schools to limit students’ access to the company’s AI tools. But if schools opt out of AI altogether, they’ll also lose access to Google Search.
articles.body: Google is rolling out new controls for schools to limit students’ access to the company’s AI tools. But if schools opt out of AI altogether, they’ll also lose access to Google Search. The policy change could mark a major shift in how students and educators interact with one of the biggest providers of education technology in the world. Google’s Chromebook laptops are used by tens of millions of students, sometimes starting in kindergarten. The move comes as many communities have pushed for stricter limits on screen time and AI use in schools, amid growing fears that the technology could stunt students’ learning and development or pose safety risks. A number of school districts, including New York City and Los Angeles public schools, banned generative AI tools for many or all students this school year. Google on Tuesday said its products that use AI, like its Gemini assistant and Google Search, will be off by default for K-12 student accounts, until school administrators “explicitly turn them on.” The change reverses an earlier move by Google in August to turn on Gemini by default in its Google Classrooms app. But now, if schools want to turn off AI entirely, they’ll also lose access to Google Search. The company said the changes are in response to calls from educators and policymakers for more control over AI tools. Chris Phillips, vice president of education at Google, told the New York Times that “search and A.I. are deeply integrated,” and that schools that ban AI “will not have access to search, and they’ll see a message from their school that indicates it’s not available.” Google has made AI central to Search in recent years — adding “AI overviews” summarizing answers at the top of many results pages and expanding the size of the search bar to accommodate longer queries. Google’s Tuesday blog post does not offer specifics on how these controls will work, or what students might see if they tried to access Google Search from a school that has banned AI. Phillips wrote in the post that the company will “share more specifics with schools in the coming months ahead of the changes rolling out so they have time to prepare and enable a smooth transition.” In response to questions from CNN about how the new controls would work, Google pointed to a Tuesday afternoon post on X in which the company said the policy change would give schools “more choice, not less.” It added that schools would be able to toggle on Gemini, Gemini Notebook and Search individually. But the post still implies that schools will not be able to use Search without AI features, saying: “AI Mode and AI Overviews will offer step-by-step guided learning through problems, so that students don’t get quick answers to schoolwork.” The policy change came as part of a larger announcement by Google about a slate of updates to its AI tools for learning, based on the idea that the technology should help students work through problems rather than simply giving them answers. Under this new “guided learning” principle, Google says that when its systems detect, for example, that a student is using Search for homework help, they’ll be prompted to walk through the problem or topic step-by-step rather than receiving a single answer. It’s an approach also being taken by other AI companies, as they seek to convince educators and parents that their products are valuable learning tools, and that experience with AI in school is essential to success in the workforce later. OpenAI in August announced “ChatGPT for Teens” which, in addition to safety controls, focuses heavily on learning, allowing parents and teens to turn on “Study Mode” to work through questions. Many tech companies have also provided funding to train teachers in AI. New York Mayor Zohran Mamdani, who announced the New York Public Schools AI ban this year, responded to Google’s policy change by accusing the company of trying to “force” AI into schools. “No corporation should have the power to dictate how we teach our children,” he said in an X post Tuesday.

articles.title: CrowdStrike announces 'kill switch' for AI agents that go rogue
articles.summary: CrowdStrike has agreed to buy two AI security startups for a combined purchase price of $495 million, according to the Wall Street Journal.
articles.body:
What happened: CrowdStrike ( CRWD ) announced a 'kill switch' for AI agents, sending its shares up more than 1% on Tuesday. The cybersecurity company also agreed to buy two AI security startups. The combined purchase price for both is $495 million , according to the Wall Street Journal.

What's behind the move: CrowdStrike said it developed a ' Kill Switch ' in Falcon Guardian , giving security teams control over AI agents. If an agent deviates from its intended behavior, a defender can terminate it wherever it runs, prevent it from launching again, and cut off its access to the enterprise network.

"AI safety is how you get the full benefit of AI. When you deploy agents with a kill switch, you stay in control," said George Kurtz, CEO and founder of CrowdStrike, in a press release.

What else you need to know: CrowdStrike also announced on Tuesday that it has signed an agreement to acquire Fiddler AI, a startup that develops tools that help companies track their AI systems.

The company also announced an agreement to acquire Dreadnode, a startup that develops tools to test AI systems for security vulnerabilities. CrowdStrike said the technology will enable its Falcon platform to continuously scan AI models, applications, and agents for potential security weaknesses before deployment.

Despite concerns earlier this year that AI would disrupt traditional business models, cybersecurity companies have instead benefited from the rise of agentic AI, which is driving increased demand for verification and authentication.

articles.title: AMD stock rises after Q3 earnings beat, as data center revenue climbs 97%
articles.summary: AMD reported its third quarter earnings after the bell Tuesday.
articles.body:
AMD ( AMD ) reported its third quarter results after the bell on Tuesday, beating expectations on the top and bottom lines, as the company's data center revenue grew 97%.

AMD stock climbed more than 7% following the news.

"Demand for our Instinct and EPYC products continued to strengthen, and we expect growth to accelerate further in the fourth quarter as we scale Helios and 'Venice' production," CEO Lisa Su said in a statement.

"With our leadership product portfolio and deep customer and supply chain relationships, we are confident in our ability to sustain very strong revenue growth and expanding profitability over the coming years."

For the quarter, AMD saw earnings per share (EPS) of $2.09 on revenue of $13.38 billion. Analysts were projecting EPS of $1.97 on revenue of $13.08 billion, according to Bloomberg consensus estimates.

The company saw EPS and revenue of $1.20 and $9.2 billion, respectively, in the same period last year.

AMD's Data Center arm generated sales of $8.5 billion, ahead of estimates of $8.19 billion. It reported revenue of $4.34 billion in the same period last year.

AMD's Client business revenue, which includes PC sales, hit $2.9 billion. Wall Street was looking for $3.06 billion.

The chipmaker's gaming business sales, however, came in at $773 million, down 40% year over year. Analysts were estimating revenue of $655 million.

The company's gaming division includes products ranging from PC graphics cards to custom silicon for game consoles. Both categories are facing higher prices due to the ongoing memory and storage shortage, depressing customer demand.

AMD's report comes after rival Intel reported better-than-anticipated Q3 results , but issued guidance well below analysts' projections last week. The news sent Intel stock plummeting nearly 29% .

The company blamed the outlook on a worse-than-anticipated decline in the PC market.

The industry is contending with two overlapping factors: difficult comparisons to last year, when Microsoft ended support for Windows 10, forcing enterprises to purchase newer Windows 11 systems, and the steady increase in PC prices, which is eating into demand.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Centre is on course to monetise land worth Rs 15,000 crore belonging to central public sector enterprises (CPSEs) during the current financial year through National Land Monetisation Corporation (NLMC), with transactions amounting to Rs 9,000 crore already finalised so far this year, an official told TOI.The land monetisation pipeline for this year includes properties of troubled telecom twins BSNL and MTNL, apart from Rashtriya Ispat Nigam (RINL), defunct Hindustan Machine Tools (HMT), ITL and Hindustan Insecticides (HIL), among others.The NLMC is also targeting additional monetisation of MTNL properties worth Rs 5,000-6,000 crore over the next two years. The telecom PSU, with operations in Delhi and Mumbai, has prime land, including apartments and office complexes. It had identified properties for disposal several years ago but progress has been slow. The telecom company, which has been taken over by BSNL, carries a substantial debt burden, with outstandings of around Rs 10,000 crore, according to the official. BSNL also is not out of the woods either, despite govt pumping in thousands of crores for "strategic reasons".The official said that while transactions of Rs 9,000 crore have been finalised, money is yet to flow in, with more properties targeted to be put up for sale in the remaining months of 2026-27.On Tuesday, NLMC organised a pre-bid meeting for the e-auction of a land parcel owned by HIL in Delhi at a reserve price of Rs 829 crore."A number of CPSEs reached out to NLMC, after it successfully e-auctioned 180 plots of RINL in Visakhapatnam in two phases, with the first phase netting Rs 366 crore against a reserve price of Rs 312 crore," NLMC CEO Rohan Thakur told reporters at the event. HIL chairperson and MD Kuldeep Singh told TOI that the next move will see sale of a residential land parcel in the city, which is in vicinity of one currently under auction.Set up in 2022 as part of govt's broader effort to put underutilised public assets to productive use, NLMC functions under the finance ministry and is mandated to monetise non-core land assets of CPSEs and govt agencies. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ahead of the pre-budget consultation with revenue secretary Arvind Shrivastava on Wednesday, industry bodies were working out their final wish list on long-term capital gains tax (LTCG) - the most-discussed budgetary proposal this year.Executives at industry associations said that there were competing views from members and tax experts and a final call on how the demand should be worded was yet to be taken. While the proposal is not completely new, it has got a major thrust amid stagnant stock market indices and negative returns for foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) due to a weak rupee. The call gained further momentum after the Centre scrapped the 12.5% long-term capital gains tax on FPI investment in govt securities in June as part of a strategy to support the rupee.On Tuesday, while some of the bodies were finetuning their position, most strident were FPIs, demanding that govt abolish the tax at least for them. So, some industry representatives have suggested that short-term capital gains tax and securities transaction tax (STT) be retained in their current form and LTCG in year 1 also be left unchanged at 12.5%. But those who hold the shares longer should be charged concessional LTCG, which could fall to zero over three-five years.There is also a school of thought that STT should be abolished and LTCG be retained. articles.body:
How does inflation compare to past midterm cycles?

Kitchen table issues typically drive voters’ decisions at the ballot box, and this year will be no different.

Americans have been grappling with inflation running above 2 percent for five and a half years, with prices in September up 3.7 percent annually , according to the consumer price index (CPI).

Annual inflation is up from February, when it was 2.4 percent . On the last day of that month, the U.S. and Israel launched the war with Iran — which sparked a surge in fuel prices in the U.S., impacting drivers, truckers and farmers.

Here is where inflation stood in October of the last five midterm years, based on the CPI, and what happened in those elections.

Inflation surged in 2021 and 2022 , as an explosion in COVID-19 era government spending, supply chain shortages and the Russian invasion of Ukraine sent prices soaring.

Democrats went into the 2022 midterms in control of both chambers of Congress. That November, Republicans narrowly snatched control of the House, but Democrats held on to control of the Senate.

Inflation in October 2018 was exactly where it stood in January 2017, the month of President Trump’s first inauguration . Annual inflation sunk to 1.6 percent in June 2017 but rose above 2 percent by the end of that year.

In the first midterms after Trump’s 2016 presidential victory, Democrats won a net of 41 House seats to flip control of the lower chamber. The GOP, meanwhile, expanded its majority in the Senate by two seats.

Inflation remained in the 1 percent to 2.1 percent range from May 2012 through December 2016, as the economy recovered from the aftereffects of the 2008 financial crisis.

In 2014, Republicans expanded their majority in the House by 13 seats and flipped the Senate. That gave the GOP control of Congress as former President Obama wound down his second term.

Inflation dipped below into negative territory in 2009, as the economy slowly regained its footing after the crash.

While Democrats held on to the Senate despite Republicans gaining six seats that year, the GOP rode Tea Party momentum to a whopping 63-seat gain en route to House control.

Inflation dipped from 2.1 percent in September 2006 to 1.3 percent that October.

But voters still punished Republicans and former President George W. Bush , as Democrats campaigned against the unpopular Iraq War to flip both chambers of Congress.

articles.title: CVS Health moves to dismantle $117bn healthcare empire
articles.summary: CVS Health is plotting a break-up of its $117bn healthcare empire, separating its retail pharmacy chain from its insurance business in what would...
articles.body:
CVS Health is plotting a break-up of its $117bn healthcare empire, separating its retail pharmacy chain from its insurance business in what would be one of the largest corporate splits of all time.

The move would unwind CVS's $78bn acquisition of health insurance company Aetna in 2018, which created a vertically integrated healthcare conglomerate spanning an insurer, a pharmacy benefit manager and a retail pharmacy.

Under plans being discussed, CVS would spin off its retail pharmacy division, whose 9,000 drugstores are projected to generate a third of the group's $417bn in revenue this year, as a separate listed company, according to people familiar with the matter.

The break-up would come as the industry faces intense political pressure challenging combined ownership of PBMs, which manage drug prescription benefits on behalf of insurers, employers and pharmacies.

The company could announce the move as early as its third-quarter results this week, the people said. Insurer Aetna and Caremark, CVS's PBM, would remain together under one corporate entity as part of the plans under consideration, they added.

The structure and timeline of the break-up were still in flux and could yet change, the people warned. CVS did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Shares in CVS have bounced back under the leadership of David Joyner, who started as chief executive in October 2024, driven by a turnaround at its Aetna insurance unit. Its stock sank to a 10-year low in December 2024. CVS's market value stood at $116.9bn at Tuesday's close, more than double where it was trading at its nadir.

CVS is fighting states' legislation to ban companies from owning PBMs and pharmacies. Lawmakers in Arkansas and Tennessee were the first two states to introduce such measures.

Earlier this year, Tennessee's state legislature passed the Fair Rx Act banning ownership of pharmacies by companies which run both a PBM and insurer. CVS and its rival Cigna have sued to try to block the measure, which is set to take effect in 2028. In Arkansas, a judge blocked the law, introduced in April last year, pending further review.

These changes have gained widescale support from both sides of the aisle in Washington. In the US Senate, Democrat Elizabeth Warren and Republican Josh Hawley recently reintroduced bipartisan legislation to prohibit PBM and pharmacy co-ownership.

CVS has led the charge as the wider health insurance industry emerges from a period of financial strain. Cost controls have boosted margins at the health insurance unit just as the US government also increased payment rates for Medicare insurance plans. Even CVS's name-brand drugstores, a laggard of the wider business, benefited from a jump in profits and revenues in the first half of the year.

articles.title: WNBA Finals Game 7 becomes W's most-watched playoff game, with Valkyries' title-clinching win drawing 3.3 million viewers
articles.summary: Golden State gave its fans a Halloween scare, scoring only 24 first-half points before rallying to finish the first-ever WNBA Finals Game 7 on top, defeating...
articles.body:
The first-ever WNBA Finals Game 7 delivered on Saturday night.

While trick-or-treaters were out hunting for candy, a 68-63 Golden State Valkyries title-clinching victory proved popcorn-worthy.

Natalie Nakase's squad rallied on Halloween to take down the Atlanta Dream , and the must-watch showdown at San Francisco's Chase Center averaged 3.3 million viewers on USA Network, CNBC and Peacock, becoming the most-watched WNBA playoff game ever and the second most-watched WNBA game, period, since the league's opening weekend in 1997.

Gabby Williams put up a 30-piece, scoring a WNBA postseason-record 28 second-half points and giving her Valkyries a shot in the arm after they trailed 30-24 at the break. Williams, this year's Finals MVP , ultimately powered Golden State to a monumental victory over Angel Reese, Allisha Gray, Rhyne Howard and the rest of the Dream at Ballhalla.

In a matchup of two franchises searching for their first-ever league championship, the nascent Valkyries — just in their second season of existence — came out on top.

The Dream, currently led by Karl Smesko, have now lost in the Finals each of the four times they've advanced that far. It was their first appearance in the Finals since 2013.

This season was only the second in league history that featured a best-of-seven Finals. The W expanded the series from a best-of-five in 2024, first implementing the change last season. But the 2025 campaign ended somewhat unceremoniously, with the Las Vegas Aces sweeping the Phoenix Mercury in four games .

In 2026, the WNBA got the full best-of-seven experience , featuring not only its first-ever Game 7 but also, in the process, its first-ever Game 6.

Notably, the timing of Game 6 was hotly debated after scheduling complications resulted in the contest starting at 12:30 p.m. ET last Thursday.

Back then, the Valkyries had a 3-2 lead in the series and were on the road. The early tip-off stemmed from a conflict that was pervasive throughout the series. In order to continue to play Dream home playoff games at State Farm Arena, they had to work around the venue's prior commitments, including those to the NBA's Hawks.

When it came to Game 6, that iteration of Valkyries-Dream had to be played early — that is, if it was going to take place on Thursday, due to a previously scheduled Hawks game that night. The compromise was scrutinized, leading to a Dream ownership clarifying that, on multiple occasions, it had raised concerns about the matter .

Nevertheless, despite all of that controversy, Game 6 still generated relatively impressive viewership numbers . In fact, the Dream's series-extending 80-69 victory went down as the fifth most-watched WNBA Finals game on cable to date, according to USA Sports PR.

As a whole, the series zigged and zagged, with Golden State taking Games 1, 4, 5 and 7, whereas Atlanta wound up winning Games 2, 3 and 6. Along the way, Reese — one of the biggest names in the sport — piled up four double-doubles, the second most a player has recorded in a single WNBA Finals .

In the end, though, a well-rounded Valkyries team wore the crown, after Williams starred in an eye-catching winner-take-all game on Saturday.
